min_stable_gain.conditions: p3 table 'Gain of +7 stable FET Input'; p14 'minimum recommended gain of +7'
min_stable_gain.below_min_gain_guidance: p14: for lower noninverting gains consider OPA656 or OPA659. p15-17 (9.1.3, Figs 31/32): low-gain inverting operation with external compensation, where C_S from the inverting node to ground and C_F across R_F set the high-frequency noise gain NG2 = 1 + C_S/C_F above the minimum stable gain. Example: R_G = 250 ohm, R_F = 500 ohm, C_F = 2.9 pF, C_S = 27 pF, NG1 = 3, NG2 = 10.5, G = -2 V/V, measured -3 dB at 170 MHz. p18: with a matched 50 ohm source the inverting minimum stable gain becomes -12 V/V (equivalent GBP 3.2 GHz). p21: 'Unity-gain stability in the operational amplifier is not required for application as a transimpedance amplifier.'

tia_content.noise: 1.8 pA/rtHz total equivalent input noise current over 10 MHz

tia_content.C_F: 0.55 pF total (0.4 pF physical + 0.1 pF resistor parasitic + about 50 fF PCB)
tia_content.C_D_or_source_C: 49 pF diode + 0.3 pF PCB (+ 0.7 + 4.5 pF amplifier input)
tia_content.bandwidth: Table 1 target 1 MHz. A Butterworth design (Eq 7) would need the feedback pole at 3.5 MHz, i.e. a total C_F of 0.2 pF, which the text calls hard to achieve. Eq 8 gives about 4.8 MHz closed-loop bandwidth. With C_F raised to 0.55 pF the simulated bandwidth is 1.7 MHz with about 82 deg phase margin.
tia_content.noise: measured (Fig 35) and simulated (Fig 36) output noise: 60 nV/rtHz at low frequency (0.3 pA/rtHz input-referred; R_F dominates, amplifier negligible), peaking at about 440 nV/rtHz near 5-6 MHz (CURVE: measured 437 nV/rtHz at 5 MHz, 409 at 10 MHz, 145 at 50 MHz)
tia_content.pulse: 5 uA pulse gives 239 ns rise and 224 ns fall (Fig 37); 0.5 V on the 50 ohm scope input

tia_content.Eq7: 1/(2 pi R_F C_F) = sqrt(GBP/(4 pi R_F C_D)) for Butterworth
tia_content.Eq9: V_OUTN = sqrt((I_N R_F)^2 + 4kTR_F + E_N^2 + (E_N 2 pi C_D R_F F)^2/3)

application_guidance: Keep R_F || R_G < 150 ohm for voltage gain. About 0.2 pF shunts a typical resistor, so above 1.5 kOhm it adds a pole or zero below 500 MHz. TIA designs may use any R_F if C_F accounts for all inverting-node parasitics. Open the ground and power planes under the signal I/O pins. Put 0.1 uF decoupling within 0.1 in (power-supply section) or 0.25 in (layout section), plus 2.2-6.8 uF bulk; an optional capacitor between the supplies improves HD2. Do not use sockets. More than 2 pF of parasitic load can degrade performance; use an R_S per Fig 17 (about 48 ohm at 30 pF, 18 ohm at 200 pF) (p14, p18-19, p24-26).
abs_max_and_input_protection: Supply +/-6.5 V. Differential and common-mode input -V_S to +V_S. T_J 175 C; storage -65 to 125 C. ESD: HBM 2000 V, CDM 500 V, MM 200 V. Internal diodes to both supplies on all pins carry about 30 mA continuous; add series input resistors if higher currents are possible (p4, p13).
other_notes: The typical-characteristic plots refer to 'See Figure 28' for the test circuit, but Figure 28 is the ESD diagram and the test circuits are Figures 29 and 30.
The effective load is 83 ohm for the Fig 29 test circuit (p14).
p1: 'high 1.6-GHz gain bandwidth product gives greater than 10-MHz signal bandwidths up to gains of 160 V/V (44 dB)'.

High-grade (UB) DC specs (p7): V_OS 0.1 typ / 0.6 max mV; drift 2 typ / 6 max uV/C; I_B 1 typ / 5 max pA (450 pA at 0-70 C, 1250 pA at -40 to 85 C); CMRR 98 typ / 91 min dB; +PSRR 82 / 78 dB; -PSRR 74 / 68 dB.
Worst-case dissipation example: P_D = 236 mW, T_J = 121 C for SOT-23 at 85 C (p27).
